ruling: R41 (Drew, 2026-09-15): a Pokémon JA pool row whose slug year is not the set's RELEASE year is re-keyed onto the release year.
reportOnlyUntil: REPORT ONLY until a steward dispatches it. This file routes nothing by existing; the lane writes only under BACKFILL_APPLY=true.
finding: 5,306 rows sit in a (year, setKey) cell that is NOT their set's release year, while the checklist for that set sits in exactly one cell — the release year. They were reading as "destination not checklist-backed" when the checklist exists, one year away.
rulings: THE RELEASE YEAR IS THE PRODUCT'S YEAR. Each staged tcgdex-ja-modern manifest carries its set's year and the catalog holds that set in exactly ONE cell. A row on the same set code in any other year is in the wrong cell.

THE DRIFT IS A SALE/GRADING YEAR, NOT A PRODUCT YEAR. These are December releases whose sales and gradings fall in the following year. The census carries the proof: a row TITLED "2023 POKEMON JPN SV4A-SHINY TREASURE EX S #294 KINGAMBIT PSA 10" is stored at pokemon:2024 — its own title says 2023. Same class as the hobbymonitor publication-year and vintage sale-year-slug findings.
ONLY WHERE THE DESTINATION IS CHECKLIST-BACKED. A set whose release-year cell holds no checklist row is skipped, not forced.
SPLIT-IDENTITY ROWS ARE EXCLUDED: where cardId disagrees with hobbyiqCardId on the vertical or the set code, the row is left for the split-identity lane.
TWO SHAPES, as in R34/R35/R39: slug cardId -> RELOCATE (the year is in the partition key, so the row really moves); opaque vendor cardId -> REPOINT (hobbyiqCardId patched in place, #1941 guard runs).

census.note: read from prod read-only on 2026-09-15, paged by (sport, year, setKey) slug prefix; no cross-partition COUNT was issued over sold_comps.
